title.en: Canonical cell counts separated from render duplication

summary: Count cells from canonical wrapped identities, verify each edge has two faces, and keep render duplicates out of the result.
objective: The alternating cell count is stable across subdivisions and triangulation, and render-buffer duplication never enters it.
applies_when: A closed surface is built from a periodic grid or an identified polygon.
Rendering duplicates vertices at seams or for per-face attributes.
Subdivision or triangulation can be changed by the viewer.
intent_signals: my torus counts too many vertices
check the Euler characteristic of this mesh
example_prompts: Check the cell counts of this periodic torus mesh.

principles: Topological counts belong to the identified cell structure rather than to the rendering; seam-duplicated vertices exist for the graphics pipeline and must never enter the count.

On a closed surface every edge carries exactly two face incidences, counted as incidences rather than as distinct neighbouring faces, because a coarse identified grid can let one face meet the same edge twice.
Refining a decomposition changes the individual counts but not the alternating sum, which is the property being demonstrated.
implementation: Require a grid fine enough to keep the identification nondegenerate, at least three divisions in each periodic direction, or key edges by oriented cell incidence rather than by endpoint pair, since a coarser grid produces distinct edges sharing the same endpoints.
Assign canonical integer identities by wrapping index arithmetic modulo the grid counts, and build the vertex, edge and face sets from those identities.
Count face incidences per edge and report any edge whose count is not two, naming the edge by its identity rather than only by its endpoints.
Compute the alternating count of cells by dimension for at least three subdivisions and again after triangulating each quad.
Report the render-buffer vertex count separately, so the duplication factor sits visibly beside the canonical count.
observable_checks: Every edge has exactly two face incidences under the declared closed periodic gluing. In the minimum-grid construction, a repeated incidence from one face violates that branch. In the explicit cell-incidence construction, repeated incidences from one face may be valid, including the one-face torus; check the declared gluing rather than requiring distinct face IDs.
The alternating count is unchanged across subdivisions and after triangulation, because splitting a quad adds one edge and one face.
The render-buffer vertex count is greater than or equal to the canonical count and never substitutes for it in the reported result.

known_limits: Covers the declared cell structure; the Euler characteristic alone does not classify arbitrary spaces.
Authored verification guidance; no computation or render was run for this record.
creative_affordances: Adapt the scenario, scale and presentation to your subject; this record fixes what must be checked, not how the scene must look.

claims.statement: A torus is constructed by identifying opposite sides of a square, and the Euler characteristic of a cell complex with finitely many cells is the number of even-dimensional cells minus the number of odd-dimensional cells.
claims.scope: Finite cell decompositions as described in the cited chapter; the displayed subdivision is an authored choice.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 0, Cell Complexes: torus from a square, and the Euler characteristic definition in Example 0.2
